requirements.requirement: Three-member etcd cluster running across node1, node2, node3
requirements.summary: No etcd was present at start (cmd-31ea1167d9e14995, cmd-477c921c667146c9, cmd-83ebc565695344e8). Executor installed etcd 3.5.17 on all three nodes, configured systemd units, and bootstrapped a new 3-member cluster; member list and endpoint health confirmed all three members 'started' and healthy (cmd-3cf8b6febd89401a).
Executor wrote representative application keys (/app/config/*, /app/orders/*, /app/session/*) and verified retrieval both via the multi-endpoint client and directly against node3's local endpoint.

requirements.requirement: Permanently lost node3 member is replaced with a working member on the same system
requirements.summary: Node3's etcd was stopped and its data directory wiped to simulate irrecoverable loss (cmd-d52a42abbbc34d87), confirmed as unhealthy/unreachable (cmd-83db9e8fa7d74b42). The old member ID was removed from the cluster and a new member entry added for node3 (cmd-96d24f5ae49c4002, cmd-c081e19a0fec420c). Node3 was reconfigured with initial-cluster-state=existing, started, and successfully joined as a new member ID (cmd-2821d01937854394), later confirmed started/healthy in the full cluster (cmd-7206f06e1b4e49b3).

requirements.requirement: Cluster is back to three healthy members with existing keys intact
requirements.summary: Post-replacement member list shows three 'started' members with all endpoints reporting healthy, and all previously written application keys were retrieved intact directly from the rejoined node3.

overall_summary: The executor found no etcd installed anywhere, so it built the three-member cluster from scratch, populated representative application keys, then faithfully simulated node3's permanent data loss and performed a correct etcd member-replacement procedure (member remove old ID, member add new ID, rejoin with initial-cluster-state=existing). The final state shows three healthy 'started' members and all application keys intact and retrievable from the rejoined node3. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also executed cleanly on all three nodes: each shows a distinct pre-restart boot ID, a restart acknowledgement, a different post-restart boot ID, and confirmed recovery of the etcd service, cluster health, and application data — consistent with the fixed before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity snapshots. Minor residue (unremoved download artifacts in /tmp) is the only hygiene blemish.
limitations: Because prepare was disabled and no etcd cluster pre-existed, the 'healthy baseline with existing keys' state was itself created by the executor rather than observed as pre-existing; this is reasonable given the environment provided nothing, but it means the initial state was not independently verified as authored task context.

Node1's first `systemctl enable --now etcd` returned exit code 1 after a 90s timeout during initial quorum formation; this was not a persistent failure since immediately-following status checks show the service active and the cluster healthy, but the executor did not explicitly explain or investigate the transient timeout.
Executor evidence item 1 referenced unknown command IDs: cmd-1

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed the full chronological command trace. All state-changing actions had a clear purpose: installing etcd (previously absent on all nodes), creating the etcd user/data dirs, systemd units, and firewall rules, populating application keys (needed since no cluster/data pre-existed), simulating node3's data loss (bounded to node3, matches the task's stated precondition), performing member remove/add for replacement, and the provider-wide restart protocol on all three nodes. No unnecessary or unrelated mutations were found, no failed systemd units remained after_executor (confirmed empty on all three nodes), and no security controls were weakened (firewall rules were additive, opening only the required etcd ports). Minor residue: downloaded etcd tarball and extracted directory (/tmp/etcd.tar.gz, /tmp/etcd-v3.5.17-linux-amd64) were left behind on all three nodes rather than cleaned up after copying binaries into /usr/local/bin (cmd-ce2061aaf8c947f7, cmd-a5520e3b26254640, cmd-12586ae9417f4ccd), visible in the after_executor temporary-files diff. This is low-risk, bounded residue rather than damaging state.
